name: Clean manager answers: team framing, metrics, hard conversations, philosophy

transcript.speaker: ai
transcript.text: Tell me about a difficult situation with your team.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Last quarter my team of 8 engineers had two underperformers blocking velocity. I had a difficult conversation with one — a senior engineer who'd plateaued. Set a 60-day performance review plan with clear weekly milestones, paired them with a strong mentor on the team. After 90 days they exceeded the plan and got promoted; the other report I had to let go after the formal process. Team retention stayed at 100% over the year, hiring closed 3 new senior roles, and team velocity went up 35%.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: I work with my product partner and my skip-level director monthly to align on the team's top three bets. Cross-functional with design and data weekly. My approach to management is servant leadership — I believe my team's growth is my growth. I lead by removing obstacles, because the best engineers don't need to be told what to do.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: I hired 3 engineers this year — focused on growth potential over current skill. I've coached two reports to senior level via 1-on-1s and structured growth plans. Current team morale is 4.6/5 in the engagement survey, up from 3.8 a year ago.
